At **JP Morgan Chase**, Matt was Technology Delivery Lead for ACCESS Next Generation from **August 2009** to **June 2012**. The bank was consolidating regional treasury and cash-management systems into a unified global portal, but Bottomline Technologies’ WebSeries platform could not meet its requirements out of the box. Payment types had different formatting, validation, compliance, and approval requirements. Legacy connectivity was fragmented, and entitlement changes took days of manual configuration.

Matt managed a **40+** blended **Accenture** and bank team across the US, Mumbai, and Bangalore, spending **70 to 80%** of his time embedded at Bottomline’s Portsmouth offices. He designed and delivered bespoke ACH, wire, FX/cross-border, and tax-payment modules. The work included NACHA file validation, integration with the bank’s foreign exchange engine, and Message Authentication Code security so corporate users could verify payment integrity before release.

He also designed the centralized payments gateway, handling message transformation, protocol translation, and routing across **12 countries**. Rather than build separate regional platforms, he mapped jurisdiction-specific requirements into data visibility, access controls, and configuration within a single global architecture, sequencing regional launches by regulatory readiness.

For corporate administrators, Matt introduced bulk permission changes across users, accounts, and products from a single screen. Payment-specific controls could authorize someone to approve wires without permitting FX initiation. Entitlement management dropped from **days to minutes**.

He led payments data migration while preserving client configurations, transaction histories, and compliance traceability, with **zero disruption to live payment operations**. He also owned on-call and critical production incident response.

ACCESS launched in **April 2011**, serving **135,000+ clients** across **180+ countries**. The gateway gave corporate treasurers a single entry point for wire, ACH, and cross-border transfers, replacing separate local logins and regional payment systems.

He translated regional regulatory requirements into data-visibility and access controls, sequencing launches by regulatory readiness rather than a single global deployment. Matt leads with empathy, clarity, and purpose. Across the engineering teams he inherited, the recurring problem was teams that were “over-processed, under-trusted, waiting for permission instead of owning outcomes.” At **Accenture**, his work ranged from modern engineering initiatives to leading a **150-person** Cloud Innovation Center. His focus was creating an environment where engineers, designers, and product teams could do the best work of their careers.

He makes intent explicit, pushes decisions to the people closest to the work, and uses transparency, direct feedback, and open communication. He coaches teams to think clearly, not just execute tasks. His non-negotiables include psychological safety, integrity and respect, outcomes rather than optics, and continuous learning.

That includes a “permit to fail” learning environment. When teams avoided risks because they feared blame, Matt organized non-punitive post-mortems and supported lean, low-stakes experiments with structured hypotheses and controlled iterations. In product incubation, he set expectations that early prototypes and user tests would likely fail intentionally: teams were testing assumptions before committing to costly builds. Post-mortem learnings went into subsequent sprints to prevent repeat failures.

He also built balanced teams with engineers, product managers, and UX architects sharing accountability, rather than working through hierarchical handoffs. Daily practices included pair programming, collaborative coding, retrospectives, automation, and continuous delivery.

At the Cloud Innovation Center, teams achieved **4x delivery acceleration** once they embraced lean product and modern engineering practices. In the balanced-team work, teams reduced project delays and achieved **zero-defect production code** through iterative development and real-time feedback loops.

Matt’s work spans execution and delivery, organizational transformation, and talent development: enterprise platforms, cloud-native systems, and the engineering organization that builds them. They needed to move beyond waterfall delivery and siloed teams, while still meeting enterprise security, compliance, and governance requirements.

Matt built the Atlanta and Tampa Cloud Innovation Centers from **0** to **150+ practitioners**, with full P&L accountability. Instead of presenting slides about the methodology, he invited clients to observe standups, pairing, and teams solving problems together.

At **Capital One**, slow iterations and misaligned priorities were extending time-to-market. Matt formed an **8-person** cross-functional team and introduced a client-prioritized, testable backlog with disciplined red-green-refactor practice. The team delivered features **3 to 4 times faster** than other **Accenture** teams on the same engagement, with **zero production defects**. The client sought to retain the team beyond its planned end.

Across the CIC, teams achieved **4X faster velocity** and **zero-defect deployments**, delivering **30+ product engagements** across **15+ Fortune 500 clients**. Delivery excellence and customer relationships contributed to **\$100M+ in repeat business**. Matt’s earlier work included **JP Morgan Chase** payments and Salesforce platforms, each rolled out across **12 countries**.

question: Why hire Matt?

answer_md:
🐾 Here’s a time Matt failed, and what happened afterward.

Matt was the tech lead on a global platform modernization delivery for a financial services client. The program was under delivery pressure, with offshore teams executing test cycles across development, QA, UAT, and production. IAM controls, environment segregation, and downstream access configurations had been inherited from prior phases, along with existing documentation.

Matt was responsible for ensuring a safe environment setup. Instead of verifying the configuration, he assumed the IAM controls and environment boundaries were correct. He relied on the inherited documentation, did not audit who could trigger downstream jobs or email processes, and did not verify whether production customer names and email addresses had been masked or scrubbed. He also had not implemented compensating controls such as data masking or email interception.

An offshore tester accidentally triggered an email job in UAT. It sent communications containing unmasked production customer data to **thousands of real clients**.

Matt took accountability and led the team through root cause analysis and remediation. They worked collectively to understand what happened and implement corrective controls. The root causes were insufficient IAM checks, unclear environment boundaries, and production data that had not been scrubbed from downstream environments.

The client demanded that the tester be removed from the project. Matt described that as “a systemic failure that resulted in an individual consequence.” His stated lesson was that “assumptions are risks in disguise.” Following the incident, IAM validation, environment verification, PII scrubbing, and risk ownership became day-one leadership responsibilities in his delivery approach.

🐾 Here’s how Matt built AWS Launchpad.

At **Accenture’s** Liquid Studio, traditional training programs weren’t keeping pace with rapidly evolving AWS technologies. Engineers had gaps in cloud competency, and cloud adoption was slowing. The Atlanta Innovation Hub needed a structured program that would help engineers earn certifications and prepare them to lead cloud-native transformation initiatives, rather than rely on training that wasn’t closing those gaps.

As Cloud Native Architecture Lead, Matt led AWS Launchpad from **July 2018 to November 2019**, working in collaboration with AWS to develop a tailored enablement program. He designed structured learning paths and certification programs covering AWS core services, including Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, Kubernetes, and ECS/Fargate, alongside cloud-native application development. The program connected those learning paths with AWS best practices and the work engineers would encounter on cloud projects.

Instead of relying on theory alone, Matt delivered interactive workshops and hands-on labs that immersed engineers in real-world AWS environments. He established cloud expert mentorship teams so participants could learn from experienced practitioners. He also organized group coaching sessions and knowledge-sharing workshops, bringing engineers together to exchange knowledge and reinforce practical application.

More than **200 professionals** earned AWS certifications, including AWS Solutions Architect and DevOps Engineer certifications. The program accelerated cloud adoption across **Accenture** and established mentorship, coaching, and knowledge-sharing practices to support continued learning beyond certification.
